messages.subject: Error with Maaslin on galaxy
messages.body_plain:
Dear Maaslin Users,

I'm trying to use MaAsLin on Galaxy but I am always confronted with :
1
A MaAsLin error has occurred
It typically happens when incorrect 'Last metadata row' was selected
For demo data please choose 'Weight'

I don't know if it is important for MaAsLin that the dataset not carry any blank cells...in case it is, I checked, there is no empty rows and no symbols other than _ or |. Of course, I uploaded it as a MaAsLin file.

Worryingly, i get the same error when I try with the demo data.

I tried using MaAsLin on two different Galaxy servers.

Is there anything else I should be attention to when uploading my data ?

Last question : does MaAsLin accept values with < or > ? (I deleted them from my data but it would be practical if I could use them.)

Thank you for your help !

Camille Fournier

messages.body_plain:
Hello Camille,

I just tried 2 times to run maaslin against the sample data successfully, so why don't we try to solve your problem against the sample data and go from there?

Can you upload the sample data with a data type of maaslin?
Can you run maaslin by selecting last metadata row=weight?
See enclosed screen print
Run

If it works, see what is the difference in format between your file and sample file.

Let me know....
Best regards,
George Weingart PhD
Huttenhower Lab

messages.body_plain:
Dear George,

I tried on your server and it worked ! (I still don't know why it doesn't work on the one I am usually using.)

I also checked, i was not working with my data because of some blank spaces that were inadvertently left within the dataset.

I would have a last question : is the analysis falsified by values expressed as < or >x (with x as a certain value) ?

Thank you for your help !

Best regards,

Camille

messages.subject: should i filter input to a single taxonomic rank
messages.subject_clean: should i filter input to a single taxonomic rank
messages.body_plain:
I noticed in the example files that the entire output from a classifier (like metaphlan) is used that includes classifications at kingdom, phylum, class, etc.

Perhaps this is a naive question, but in practice one should filter to a single taxonomic rank - say genus, correct?

Thanks!
james
